From the owner
The Island Is the Decision Most kitchen layouts are settled the moment the island is placed. Too small and it becomes a landing strip. Too large and the walkways choke. We generally want forty-two to forty-eight inches of clearance on working sides, and we want to know who sits there, who cooks there, and whether homework happens there before we draw a single line. Get the island right and the rest of the kitchen tends to solve itself.
